articles.body: Every directory story assumes a power law: a handful of winners take almost everything. Ours does not look like that — and the difference matters if you are the one publishing. Across 765 skills and their accumulated download counts: Share of skills (ranked by downloads) Share of all downloads Top 1% 5.6% Top 5% 20.2% Top 10% 30.7% Top 20% 48.1% Top 50% 78.8% For comparison, app-store distributions routinely have the top 1% taking 80% or more of downloads. Ours takes six percent. 19.9% of skills — 152 of them — have never been downloaded once. Why the curve is flat Three reasons, in order of how confident I am. One: the directory is young and the traffic is thin. Total downloads across the whole site are still in the low thousands.

articles.excerpt: What I Built Have you ever encountered a Python error, copied it into a search engine, opened several tabs, and still struggled to understand what went wrong? I built ErrorBite, a local AI-powered Pyt…
articles.body: What I Built Have you ever encountered a Python error, copied it into a search engine, opened several tabs, and still struggled to understand what went wrong? I built ErrorBite, a local AI-powered Python error explainer that helps developers understand errors in plain English. Instead of spending time searching through documentation and forum posts, users can paste an error message into ErrorBite and get an explanation of: Plain-English Explanation: What the error means. Likely Cause: What may have caused it. Suggested Fix: How to approach fixing it. Step-by-Step Debugging: What to check next. The goal is simple: spend less time deciphering error messages and more time writing code. ErrorBite is built with Python and Streamlit, using a locally running Ollama model for inference.

articles.title: 03.14.09, Canada's one addition to NIST SP 800-171
articles.excerpt: ITSP.10.171 is the Canadian Cyber Centre's adaptation of NIST SP 800-171 Revision 3, and the government says plainly that it doesn't change the technical content in any substantive way. It has 98 requ…
articles.body: ITSP.10.171 is the Canadian Cyber Centre's adaptation of NIST SP 800-171 Revision 3, and the government says plainly that it doesn't change the technical content in any substantive way. It has 98 requirements . NIST's Revision 3 has 97. The 1 extra is 03.14.09, dedicated administration workstation. It is the only requirement in the Canadian standard that isn't in the American one. It comes from the Canadian control catalogue, source control SI-400 in the ITSG-33 lineage, and nobody who has only worked from 800-171 will have seen it. What it asks for Three things. Administrative and superuser actions are done from a physical workstation dedicated to that work and isolated from all other functions and networks, especially the internet.
articles.author: Hans Study

articles.title: Nobody Owns the Network Between the Integrator and IT
articles.excerpt: Ask who’s responsible for the security of a building’s camera and access control network, and you’ll usually get a pause, then a deflection. The integrator says they delivered what the contract specif…
articles.body: Ask who’s responsible for the security of a building’s camera and access control network, and you’ll usually get a pause, then a deflection. The integrator says they delivered what the contract specified. The IT department says they were handed a finished system they didn’t design and can’t fully see. The facilities team says it’s a security system, so surely security owns it. The security team means guards and policy, not subnets. Everyone is partly right, which is another way of saying nobody owns it. That gap is the actual vulnerability. Not a specific unpatched camera, though there are plenty of those. The structural problem is that the network between the integrator and IT belongs to no one, and unowned infrastructure doesn’t get secured, monitored, or maintained.

articles.title: Eight Bits of Trust; eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
articles.excerpt: I remember sitting in a coffee shop, laptop open, surrounded by the comforting aroma of freshly brewed coffee, when I first stumbled upon the news that eMudhra's CA keys were cracked in mere milliseco…
articles.body: I remember sitting in a coffee shop, laptop open, surrounded by the comforting aroma of freshly brewed coffee, when I first stumbled upon the news that eMudhra's CA keys were cracked in mere milliseconds. My heart raced. Ever wondered why something so critical could be compromised so quickly? As a developer, it hit home. We put trust in technology, and to see it shattered in such a dramatic fashion raises important questions about security in the digital world. The Shocking Discovery As I dug deeper into the story, I couldn't help but feel a mix of disbelief and curiosity. eMudhra, a major player in the digital signature space, suffered a vulnerability that let attackers exploit their Certificate Authority (CA) keys. This incident made me reflect on my own experiences with security.

articles.body: Few names in the science fiction literary world carry as much weight and respect as author Alan Dean Foster. Foster famously ghost-wrote the first " Star Wars " novelization for George Lucas in 1976 and "Splinter of the Mind’s Eye" in 1978, which was intended to be a low-budget Star Wars sequel should the space opera not become a hit. articles.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.excerpt: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attac…
articles.body: Expect to see quite a few websites serving error pages today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild. Image: Shutterstock.com, Sashkin. The flaws at issue are present in PHP , the programming language that powers sites running on a large number of web publishing systems, including Drupal , Magento , Joomla and WordPress . Earlier today, PHP released an emergency security update to fix two critical bugs that can allow an attacker to execute code of their choosing on a vulnerable server.

articles.title: Science on the Space Station with NASA Astronaut Jessica Watkins
articles.excerpt: NASA astronaut and Expedition 75 flight engineer Jessica Watkins works inside the Kibo laboratory module’s Life Science Glovebox on Oct. 9, 2026, safely mixing living cell samples with a bioink and th…
articles.body: NASA/Anil Menon NASA astronaut and Expedition 75 flight engineer Jessica Watkins works inside the Kibo laboratory module’s Life Science Glovebox on Oct. 9, 2026, safely mixing living cell samples with a bioink and then filling a special cartridge with the cell‑ink mixture. The advanced research operations were part of the InSPA‑Auxilium Bioprinter‑Cell Printing investigation, which explores 3D bioprinting cartilage tissue in microgravity of higher quality than that produced on Earth. Results may advance the ability to biomanufacture cartilage, benefiting patients on Earth and crew members on long‑duration space missions. Image credit: NASA/Anil Menon
